title: Enforced Schema Invariants & Revocable Sandboxed Proxy
concept: Proxy Invariants, Revocable Proxies & Type Guards
problemStatement: Implement `createSecureSchemaProxy(schema, initialData)` that validates data against a schema on write, throws TypeErrors for unknown properties or type mismatches, and exposes a `revoke()` method that permanently disables all further read/write access.
interviewTrap: Failing to handle non-configurable or non-writable invariant checks in Proxy handlers will cause the JS engine to throw an uncatchable runtime TypeError. Revocable proxies are critical for security sandboxes.

testCases.name: Allows valid property update conforming to schema
testCases.testFn: const proxy = createSecureSchemaProxy({ name: 'string', age: 'number' }, { name: 'Alice', age: 25 }); proxy.age = 30; return proxy.age;

testCases.name: Throws TypeError on forbidden property addition
testCases.expected: Property hack is not allowed by schema
testCases.testFn: const proxy = createSecureSchemaProxy({ name: 'string' }, { name: 'Bob' }); try { proxy.hack = true; return 'no-error'; } catch (e) { return e.message; }

testCases.name: Permanently disables proxy access once revoked
testCases.testFn: const proxy = createSecureSchemaProxy({ name: 'string' }, { name: 'Eve' }); proxy.revoke(); try { const x = proxy.name; return false; } catch (e) { return true; }
